The Jayhawks may not be the most famous band to emerge from the 1970s-'80s Twin Cities scene (hello Hüsker Dü, Prince, Replacements) but they are arguably the most typically Minnesotan. listings.description:
Cast: Anne-Laure Sellier
In the 1960s, an Italian Benedictine monk claimed to have invented a machine that allowed users to see into the past, as though on a TV set. While doing research, present-day academic Béatrice becomes fascinated by this “Chronovisor,” and plunges headlong into uncovering the truth about this mysterious device. This unusual and beguiling indie perfectly captures the sensation of going down a rabbit hole of dubious arcana.

listings.description:
Cast: Gary Cooper, Clara Bow, Fredric March
A great burst of pre-code fun, Paramount on Parade was Paramount Pictures’ contribution to the all-star studio musical revue movie cycle of the early talkie years. Featuring 20 individual segments from 11 directors, the movie is literally a showcase for the incredible talents under contract: Gary Cooper, Clara Bow, Fredric March, Maurice Chavalier, Jean Arthur, Kay Francis, Jack Oakie, William Powell, Fay Wray, and lots, lots more stars.

listings.description:

High in the Alpine village of Tolzbad, any loud noise or even strong emotion risks triggering an avalanche. Consumed by a lifetime of simmering lust and repressed rivalries, one family finally erupts into a feverish torrent of sex and violence.

listings.title: WUD Film Committee Weekly Meeting
listings.description: UW-Madison students of all majors and levels of interest in film are welcome to join the WUD Film Committee—the only membership requirement is a love for movies.  WUD Film—a student-led team—hosts hundreds of diverse, innovative, and exciting movies for the University community.  Committee members help curate our film programming, manage our weekly screenings, and learn valuable leadership skills in the process.

listings.title: Dance Department Incoming Student Auditions
listings.description: Auditions are required for students wishing to pursue a degree in dance at UW-Madison. Three auditions are offered during the academic year, August, November and February. See the Dance Department website for more information.

listings.title: SoundWaves: Origins - The Spark of Life
listings.description:
In the 2026-27 academic year, SoundWaves is exploring Origins - from the start of the universe to how we developed language, join us for this four-part series as we uncover the origins of who we are. As always, each lecture is paired with live, musical performance as it relates to the theme of the evening.

In this second part, we are diving into the Spark of Life as we celebrate the 50th edition of SoundWaves. Topics include geochemistry, microbiology, and astrobiology!

listings.title: Stories Across Generations
listings.description: Settle in for a special storytime that brings generations together. Eleanor Dougherty shares beloved picture books with young listeners in a warm, welcoming setting. This gentle program invites children ages 0–8 and their caregivers to connect through stories, imagination, and the simple joy of reading together.

listings.title: Let’s Move! with Abby
listings.description: Join us for movement games and activities! From obstacle courses to dances, group games and balance activities, we’ll enjoy different opportunities to move our bodies every day. Program location is subject to change, depending on the weather. Please check our Welcome Wall for the most up-to-date location information. This event is free with general museum admission.

listings.title: Nice Age Tales
listings.description: Join us for a puppet show, songs and story time for early learners.

listings.title: Music Time with Tim
listings.description: Explore the world of music and rhythm! Each week, Tim leads children in singing and other musical activities that inspire creativity and connection. It’s an engaging experience for kids and families—free with admission.

listings.title: Li’l Music with Junko
listings.description:
Do you have a dancing baby? Discover Junko’s weekly music session where babies and toddlers can explore their natural love of rhythm. Together, you and your tiny dancer will bounce, sway, and rock with the music while learning simple rhythm patterns. They’ll build critical social skills over the weeks as they interact with new faces and watch the other babies in the room, and strengthen their bond with you through lap songs and movement activities.

It’s a wonderful way to get out of the house and connect with your baby or toddler through music and movement!

Leader Junko Yamauchi Stewart is a multitalented musician and educator, and founder of BENI Daiko Taiko Ensemble.

listings.title: Reading on the Rooftop
listings.description: Take storytime to new heights! Join Paula Panczenko on the museum rooftop for a cozy read-aloud surrounded by fresh air, gardens, and views of our Capitol and the lake. Settle in, listen to engaging picture books, and enjoy stories together in one of MCM’s most unique spaces. Bring your imagination and discover where a good book can take you!

listings.title: Messy Art with Laurie
listings.description: Join MCM art educator Ms. Laurie for a weekly burst of color, texture, and joyful experimentation. Young children can freely explore art materials in a welcoming space designed especially for our youngest artists. It’s creativity without limits—or cleanup. Come make a beautiful mess with us! Free with general admission.

listings.title: Early Explorers Playgroup
listings.description: This playgroup is expertly designed for our earliest visitors. We will provide a space for infants and toddlers (2 years and under) and their caregivers to explore and play together, and engage in unstructured play that supports various aspects of child development. Parents and caregivers will have the opportunity to connect with one another over a variety of topics. Come meet other families and make new friends!

listings.title: Dairy Air
listings.description:

What’s in the air we breathe every day? Get ready to explore the science of breathing as we learn about Wisconsin air quality and how our lungs help keep us healthy through crafts, games, and interactive activities. Depending on the day’s activities, you might walk through giant lungs, spin a prize wheel, or enjoy a lively puppet show along the way. Come discover more with us!

It’s a simple way to share a little kindness with nature!
